assertions.text: Service F055, write characteristic F057, notification characteristic F056; read is pending.
The first byte is a function code, followed by parameters. Notes permit messages up to 512 bytes.
Functions include power, streaming, bitmap, BLE configuration, splash, saving configuration and fallback configuration.
Reset-after-upload settings require save_cfg. The documented power function returns 00 for success and FF for an invalid parameter.
FEE9 is a discovery hint. Channels use d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129600 for commands, …960a for upload and …9601 for notifications.
Commands contain a length byte, ASCII command and arguments, zero-padded to 16 bytes and encrypted with AES-ECB.
The author decoded LEDON, LEDOFF, MODE, SPEED, LIGHT, DATS and DATCP.
The observed 6×12 glyph uses interleaved nibbles across nine bytes. The upload channel is unencrypted.
The Shining Mask key failed; a key found in the iDealLED project decrypted this capture.
The implementation selects MASK-prefixed names and service FFF0; command, notify and upload channels use the d44bc439 UUIDs ending 9600, 9601 and 960a.
Control commands use AES-ECB and 16-byte padding. Exact key variants need further comparison.
Commands include MODE, FC, BC, SPEED, LIGHT, IMAG, ANIM and PLAY. The README color order should be checked against the encoder.
Text uses two bitmap bytes per 16-row column, followed by three color bytes per column.
The implementation limits upload packets to 100 bytes, including two bytes of length/count overhead.
The upload state machine expects DATSOKP after DATS, REOK for chunks and DATCPOK after DATCP.
ATOTOZONE code writes handle 0x000d, despite a capture comment naming 0x000e. It subscribes to FFF1 and 2A05. Nyan notes report FFF0/FFF2/FFF1.
Frames start AA55FFFF and end with a little-endian additive 16-bit checksum. Several program and length constants remain opaque.
GIF bytes are split into 196-byte payloads; the final payload is zero-padded.
The encoder rejects more than 255 chunks, or 49,980 padded bytes. This is an implementation limit.
Reset writes are separated by 0.5 seconds. ATOTOZONE accepts any notification as a chunk receipt; Nyan notes describe stronger status checks.
Nyan notes describe an echoed index and status 00=OK, 03=bad format, 09=wrong count. The cited captures were not independently decoded here.
Nyan README says 32×32, while its protocol notes report a 64×64 grid test. ATOTOZONE identifies a 96×20 PCB.
The image implementation names service FFD0 and characteristic FFD1.
Commands use BC and 55 delimiters. The full-image builder adds no checksum; the pixel command has a position-related QQ field.
A 16×16 RGB image is traversed row-major in eight blocks of 32 pixels. Each block contains BC 0F, index+1, 96 RGB bytes and 55.
The code delays 20 ms between blocks and includes a continuous refresh path.
The README reports an earlier browser service-listing failure but also links later graffiti and image HTML clients.
Command notes name FA02 writes and FA03 notifications. Handles 6 and 9 belong to the capture. The cap README adds a 00FA service and AE00 side channel.
The total length and command are each 16-bit little-endian fields, followed by command data.
PNG command 0002 and GIF command 0003 contain file size, CRC32, screen index and raw file bytes. DIY pixel control is separate.
The documented initialization queries device information and current time, then verifies a password. Program mode precedes stored image upload.
Image replies echo the command; RET=03 means success in these notes.
The Go SendData method uses WriteWithoutResponse. Host whole-value calls do not prove browser fragmentation behavior.
Twenty device-type geometry entries are implementation hints, not twenty observed device models.
A frame contains a nine-byte header and 3,072 row-major RGB888 bytes, totaling 3,081.
The frame header is 09 0C 00 00 00 00 0C 00 00. The pixel path is 0A 00 05 01 00 R G B X Y.
The author describes a continuous stream sent over multiple chunks; detailed transport behavior remains queued.
The author reports roughly 5 FPS and occasional accumulating lag. Internal buffering is explicitly a hypothesis.
The author reports a TI CC2540F256 MCU, TTP234 touch input and an unidentified LED driver.
The Python example constructs FFF3 with fixed handles. It does not establish the service UUID here.
A pixel write is 07 02, a one-based pixel index, then R G B.
The Android author reports eight icon slots and unreadable characteristics on the tested firmware.
The Pi author reports low refresh rates and connection failures when writes are too frequent.
Packets use 8D/D8 delimiters and AB escapes. Fields include flags, device ID, command ID, sequence and optional target/source/error fields.
The implementation correlates responses using device ID, command ID and sequence. Flags control responses and processor routing.
The BOLT class uses SB-name prefixes and writes usetheforce...band to characteristic 00020005-574f-4f20-5370-6865726f2121; its TODO is retained.
IO methods implement matrix text, palette, rotation, line, fill and stored animation controls. Text is truncated to 25 characters.
The vendor matrix API accepts 8×8 palette-index frames, an RGB palette and frame rate. BOLT+ simulates the matrix on an LCD.
Service E95DD91D-251D-470A-A062-FA1922DFA9A8; matrix E95D7B77…, text E95D93EE…, delay E95D0D2D…, with the same suffix.
Five row bytes represent the 5×5 display. Bit 4 is leftmost and bit 0 rightmost; each bit is on/off.
Read/write the bitmap, write UTF-8 text and set a scrolling delay in milliseconds through separate characteristics.
The service is disabled by default. Firmware must instantiate MicroBitLEDService; BLE services consume runtime memory.
The driver uses an nRF52840; the panel uses IS31FL3741. The physical overview describes 116 LEDs and a partial 16×5 matrix with overlapping rings.
The example accepts UART text up to 50 characters through Bluefruit LE Connect and supports its color picker.
The scroller description says 18×5, while the physical overview says 16×5. Compare topology and code before normalizing.
AE00/AE01/AE02 handles authentication; A950/A951/A952/A953 handles display setup, data and acknowledgments.
The author reports a Jieli nonce/challenge/pass exchange before content. Exact chip and key are not disclosed.
The display frame uses 54, a type, big-endian length, body and additive 16-bit big-endian checksum. Types are 06 setup, 00 data and 01 complete.
A 504-byte write carries 492 payload bytes. Each data acknowledgment echoes a sequence number before the next write.
Content is a 46-byte header followed by 160×32 RGB888 pixels. The author says 128 columns are visible and 32 form a scroll buffer.
RCSP file uploads were acknowledged but did not change the display. Display content required the A9 service.
AE00 uses AE01 writes without response and AE02 notifications. A C2E6FDxx service supplies a separate FD01–FD05 control path.
Frames use FE DC BA, flag, command, big-endian 16-bit body length, body and EF.
The raw six-message authentication exchange uses a custom Jieli block cipher, explicitly described as distinct from AES.
The documented path uses 490 file bytes per 503-byte frame, CRC16/XMODEM and acknowledgment windows of eight frames.
Data sequence, window sequence, slot and offset are separate fields. Completion has additional command exchanges.
The original describes a 16-bit size and four opaque token bytes; AuraCast interprets these as a 32-bit size, CRC16 and random bytes. The documents share lineage.
DG01 exposes a 7e40 UART UUID family; the APK uses 6e40. AA00, AE00 and FEE7 also appear in its GATT inventory.
The project reports LJ733_MB_V1.1 and a manufacturer field AA01, with no verified assignee. A related watch teardown does not identify this badge chip.
Vendor UART commands use CD frames; multipart notifications require reassembly.
The upload-2 capture contains preflight and weather traffic, with no dial-start command, image chunks or completion.
The README treats 360×360 as the expected upload size; smaller probes reportedly often fail the start acknowledgment.
The Node module leaves transport external. The Home Assistant project reports model-dependent RFCOMM channels, including 1, 2 and 4.
Frames use 01, little-endian length, payload, additive 16-bit checksum and 02. The source calls the checksum CRC.
The Timebox Evo encoder uses an RGB palette and packed indices with bit reversal. Its protocol document is explicitly scoped to this model.
Animation messages carry up to 400 payload bytes outside the envelope and include a packet number.
Replies contain 01, length, 04, command, 55, payload, checksum and 02.
The README recommends staying below 30 messages per second to avoid disconnects.
Escaped 01…03 envelope; custom CRC32 and LZSS content compression.
FFF0/FFF1 and upstream writes without response with 60 ms pacing.
RGB444 with content-dependent transfer curves and eight-column tiles.
The exact iLedHat behavior remains separately scoped; chip is unknown.
Escaped 01…03 envelope; 128-byte content chunks with XOR checksum.
FFF1 endpoint; UUID alone does not distinguish the advanced line.
Column-major RGB bitplanes with the top pixel in the most significant bit.
Brightness policy and firmware applicability differ across sources.
Little-endian 16-bit length and command, with feature-specific payloads.
00FA service; FA02 writes and FA03 notification hint in the original source.
RGB888 individual pixels and a GIF path using 4,096-byte logical blocks.
The seed records a multiblock total-length prose/code contradiction and a browser fragmentation gap.
A 15-byte PNG header and standard CRC32, with handshake and receipt variants.
FA02/FA03 endpoints; the seed does not establish a service UUID.
PNG uploads; ACT1025 native text has separate evidence.
Python whole-value writes do not prove browser transfer behavior.
FE EF AA 55 framing, additive checksum and a stateful sequence token.
ISSC 49535343 UART endpoints; 138-byte application chunks and SetUTC initialization.
16×16 palette static content, AA animation and 8B uploads.
Anyka/AkOS assertions lack independent verification; opaque initialization and durability remain unresolved.

conflicts.text: Pinned Nyan README uses32×32 and questions true geometry; its notes report a64×64 grid test. Keep both; count one observed backpack line, no universal geometry.
Original MiniToo technical report says160×128 IPSLCD; vendor blog says16×16 LED. Keep contested display technology; exclude from core LED matrix totals.

Original E87 document leaves four metadata bytes as a token, while AuraCast assigns CRC/random semantics. Shared lineage does not corroborate new field interpretation. Compare original captures later.

Current open firmware supportsCH582M; README lists historicalMM32 batches and identical LSLED appearance. Hardware batch and firmware profile are separate; do not flash or assume compatibility from LSLED name.
